gloss: gerah, one twentieth of a shekel
summary: The census contribution, valuations and redemption payments all use a shekel of twenty gerahs. Ezekiel specifies the same ratio when calling for honest measures.

words.gloss: gerah, one twentieth of a shekel

senses.gloss: gerah, one twentieth of a shekel
senses.definition: A small unit of weight. Twenty make one shekel by the standard given in the biblical passages.

evidence.note: The census offering is half a sanctuary shekel, and the full shekel is defined as twenty gerahs.
The standard applies to the sanctuary valuations.
The payment for each firstborn beyond the number of Levites is five shekels at twenty gerahs to the shekel.
The same reckoning applies to redemption from a month old.
The prophet specifies twenty gerahs to the shekel alongside the reckoning of the mina.

evidence.locator: G, pp. 96–97, girû A, BE 8 3:15 and YOS 6 112

note: The Akkadian unit is usually reckoned at one twenty-fourth of a shekel. CAD also discusses a possible twelfth in one account. The biblical texts consistently specify a twentieth. The identical Hebrew spelling in the dietary laws means ‘cud’.
